name: axios
notes: Case: documentation lives in its own repository (axios/axios-docs, English pages only, last content change February 2026, archived after the docs moved into the main repo) and is checked against axios v1.20.0 (August 2026). Ground truth = statements of the docs repository that the v1.20.0 code (lib/, index.d.ts) contradicts, and request options or error codes the code has that the exhaustive lists in the docs leave out. Curated by reading lib/ and index.d.ts; the maintainers never updated this repository for these changes.

items.anchor: // `onUploadProgress` allows handling of progress events for uploads
items.what: onUploadProgress and onDownloadProgress are not browser only; the Node.js http adapter reports progress too.

items.anchor: // `adapter` allows custom handling of requests which makes testing easier.
items.what: adapter also accepts an adapter name ('xhr', 'http', 'fetch') or a list of them; the default is ['xhr', 'http', 'fetch'].
withXSRFToken (boolean or function) decides whether the XSRF token header is set, also for cross-origin requests.

items.anchor: These are the available config options for making requests.
items.what: fetchOptions passes extra RequestInit options to the fetch adapter.

items.anchor: These are the available config options for making requests.
items.what: httpVersion (1 or 2) and http2Options (e.g. sessionTimeout) enable HTTP/2 in the Node.js http adapter.

items.anchor: These are the available config options for making requests.
items.what: parseReviver is passed to JSON.parse when the response is parsed.

items.anchor: These are the available config options for making requests.
items.what: redact (config keys) and sensitiveHeaders control redaction of sensitive values in errors and logs.

items.anchor: // `socketPath` defines a UNIX Socket to be used in node.js.
items.what: allowedSocketPaths restricts which socketPath values may be used.

items.anchor: These are the available config options for making requests.
items.what: formDataHeaderPolicy ('legacy' or 'content-only') decides which headers of a form-data object are copied.
maxRate also accepts a single number for both directions.
env also accepts fetch, Request and Response implementations for the fetch adapter.

items.anchor: The table below lists out specific definitions for internal axios error.
items.what: The announced table of error codes is missing: ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, ERR_BAD_OPTION, ECONNABORTED, ETIMEDOUT, ERR_NETWORK, ERR_FR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, ERR_DEPRECATED, ERR_BAD_RESPONSE, ERR_BAD_REQUEST, ERR_CANCELED, ERR_NOT_SUPPORT, ERR_INVALID_URL, ERR_FORM_DATA_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.
